sentences.text: Final arguments heard : 16.12.2023 Date of Award : 16.12.2023  AWAR D 1.

By this award, I shall decide the present claim petition under section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act,
1988, filed by the claimants seeking compensation on account of fatal injuries sustained by deceased Shekhar Khan in a motor vehicular accident.

2. The brief facts of the case as per claim petition are that on 08.01.2022 at 08:00 p.m., Shekhar Khan (deceased herein) along with his friend Azaruddin was going on motorcycle make-Passion Pro,
bearing registration no. UP16BD-0297 and reached in front of Hojri Complex, Electricity House,
Gautam Budh Nagar, U.P. and while they were waiting there to cross the road, all of a sudden,
another motorcycle, make- Splendor bearing registration no. UP84AK-1337 (in short "offending vehicle"), being driven by respondent no.1 at a fast speed, came and hit them with a great force.
As a r e s u l t , S h e k h a r K h a n a n d A z a r u d d i n s u f f e r e d s e r i o u s ____________________________________________________________________________ injuries.
They were taken to Yatharth Hospital, Sector-10, Noida, where Shekhar Khan was declared brought dead.

In connection with the accident, FIR no.16/2022, under sections 279/338/427/304-A IPC was registered at PS Phase-II, Noida and after completion of investigation, respondent no.1 Dipender (Dipendra Singh) was charge-sheeted for commission of aforesaid offences.

By way of present claim petition, claimants alleged that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle which was being driven by respondent no.1, owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no.3 at the time of accident and thus, claimed a compensation of Rs.50 lakhs along with interest @ 12% per annum from the respondents.

3. The claim petition was found enclosed with the supporting documents viz. certified copy of FIR,
certified copy of charge-sheet, certified copy of order of release of the offending vehicle to Superdar,
certified copies of MLC and postmortem report of deceased, certified copy of site plan of the place of accident, certified copy of panchnama, certified copy of general diary of police investigation,
certified copy of mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and that of the vehicle of deceased.

Other required documents have also been found annexed with the claim petition, viz.
copies of aadhaar cards of the petitioners and aadhaar card of deceased, salary slip of deceased for the month of November-2021, driving license of deceased, insurance policy of the motorcycle of deceased and that of offending motorcycle, registration certificate of motorcycle of deceased,
registration details of the offending vehicle and that of offending motorcycle, etc.
4 . S i n c e t h e c l a i m p e t i t i o n w a s f o u n d d u l y s u p p o r t e d w i t h t h e ____________________________________________________________________________ required documents, notices were issued to the respondents.
In response to the notice, Sh. Rahul Verma Advocate appeared for respondent nos.1 and 2, whereas, Sh. S.K. Sharma Advocate appeared on behalf of the respondent no.3/ insurance company.

Written-statements was filed only on behalf of the insurance company and on the basis of pleadings of parties, issues were framed on 03.08.2023, as under:

matter was referred to Lok Adalat, scheduled for 08.10.2023 for settlement but unfortunately, the settlement proceedings could not be materialized before Lok Adalat.

Further, on 13.12.2023, learned counsels for petitioner and insurance company again showed their interest to settle the matter amicably and Sh. S.K. Sharma, learned counsel for insurance company submitted that on behalf of insurance company, he is ready to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners as per calculations on merits and filed a calculation sheet on behalf of the insurance company.

Keeping in view the same, my findings on the issues are as under:
____________________________________________________________________________ ISSUE NO.1

Whether respondent no.1was driving the offending vehicle no.
UP84AK-1337 on 08.01.2022 at about 08:00 p.m., in front of Hojri Complex Electricity House within the jurisdiction of PS Phase-II, Gautam Budh Nagar in rash and negligent manner and caused the death of deceased Sh. Shekhar Khan? OPP 6.

Since, learned counsel for the insurance company made specific endorsement on the aforesaid calculation sheet itself stating "admitted liability, award may be passed on merits as per law", I straightaway heard arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties on the quantum of compensation.
Also, I have perused the calculation sheet filed on behalf of the insurance company.

It is pertinent to mention here that as per directions given in Form-II of the new Scheme for Motor Accident Claims, formulated by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi vide judgment dated 08.01.2021 in FAO 842/2023, Rajesh Tyagi & Ors. v. Jaibir Singh & Ors., in case the amount offered by the insurance company is not acceptable to the claimants, the Claims Tribunal shall hear the arguments qua quantum of compensation and pass an award.

OPP 7.
As per calculation sheet, the insurance company offered a total compensation of Rs.34,55,267/- to the petitioners.

While computing the aforesaid compensation, insurance company considered the monthly income of deceased as Rs.16,792/-, future prospects as 40%, multiplier as ____________________________________________________________________________ Husn Bano And Ors vs Dipender And Ors on 16 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51810612/

sentences.text: Copy of above calculation was supplied to learned counsel for the petitioners, who accepted the same as it is, only except the amount of Rs.40,000/- computed under the head of loss of consortium.

Learned counsel for petitioners submitted that there are seven claimants herein, who are legal representatives of the deceased and therefore, they all are entitled to the loss of consortium of Rs.40,000/- each and therefore, petitioners are entitled to Rs.2,80,000/- (40,000x7) on account of loss of consortium instead of Rs.40,000/- only as offered by the insurer.
To examine this conflict, I have perused the claim petition and aadhaar cards of the claimants annexed thereto.

I may note that petitioner no.1 is stated to be wife of deceased,
petitioner nos.2 to 4 are stated to be children of deceased and petitioner nos. 5 to 6 are parents of deceased, whereas, petitioner no.7 Afsana is stated to be unmarried sister of deceased.

In view of decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case titled as United India Insurance Co.
Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur & Ors., Civil Appeal no. 2705 of 2020, decided on 30.06.2020, the spouse of deceased shall be entitled to spousal consortium, children shall be entitled to parental consortium and parents shall be entitled to filial consortium.

Therefore, the petitioner nos. 1 to 6 shall be entitled to Rs.2,40,000/- (40,000x6) under the head of loss of consortium.

9. Thus, after adding this amount (Rs.2,40,000/-) to the undisputed amount under the heads of loss of dependency (Rs.33,85,269/-), loss of estate (Rs.15,000/-) and funeral expenses (Rs.15,000/-),
the total compensation to which the petitioners shall be entitled comes to Rs.36,55,267/-
(33,85,269+15,000+15,000+2,40,000).

Further, the petitioners shall also be entitled to interest @
8% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
